SUMMARY: Rocky Mountain National Park Day Trip - Sky Pond via Glacier Gorge Hike
DESCRIPTION:
Denver Fun Young Adults 20s to 40s
🏔️ **SKY POND — ROCKY MOUNTAIN NATIONAL PARK**

**Saturday, November 14, 2026**

Join us for a day of hiking, incredible mountain views, and good company at Rocky Mountain National Park!

We'll take on one of the park's most scenic trails, passing waterfalls, alpine lakes, and towering peaks on our way to Sky Pond.

Come solo or bring friends. It's a great opportunity to meet new people, get outside, and enjoy some of Colorado's best scenery.

🥾 **SKY POND VIA GLACIER GORGE TRAIL**
One of the most impressive hikes in Rocky Mountain National Park! The route takes us past Alberta Falls, The Loch, and Timberline Falls before reaching Sky Pond, surrounded by the dramatic Cathedral Spires.

🥾 **\~9.5 mi • ↗️ \~1,800 ft gain • Out & Back • Hard • \~6–8+ hrs**

🗺️ **ALLTRAILS ROUTE:**
[Sky Pond via Glacier Gorge Trail](https://www.alltrails.com/explore/trail/us/colorado/sky-pond-via-glacier-gorge-trail?u=i&sh=klro7x)

🎥 **TRAIL PREVIEW:**
[Watch the Sky Pond via Glacier Gorge Video](https://youtu.be/MawC3t-r3TA?si=vKI6Vj0GSZSuL-lI)

**Hike Start:** \~9 AM

**Park Entrance:** $30 per vehicle (1-day pass). No timed-entry reservation required in November.
[Park Entrance Fees](https://www.nps.gov/romo/planyourvisit/fees.htm)

**Dogs:** Not allowed on park trails

**Restrooms:** Trailhead

🕘 **ITINERARY**
**7:00 AM** — Depart Wooly Mammoth Park-N-Ride
**\~9:00 AM** — Arrive at Glacier Gorge Trailhead and begin hiking
**\~9:45 AM** — Alberta Falls
**\~11:30 AM** — The Loch (snack and photo break)
**\~12:30 PM** — Timberline Falls (assess trail conditions)
**\~1:00 PM** — Sky Pond (conditions and daylight permitting)
**\~1:15 PM** — Begin return hike
**\~4:30–5:30 PM** — Return to trailhead
**Evening** — Return to Denver

We'll stop for lunch along the trail, so pack food, snacks, and plenty of water.

**Important:** November daylight is limited, with sunset around 4:45 PM. Reaching Sky Pond is dependent on trail conditions, hiking pace, and safe passage at Timberline Falls. We'll establish a firm turnaround time and may turn around at The Loch or Timberline Falls if needed.

🎒 **WHAT TO BRING**

* Waterproof hiking boots
* Microspikes
* Trekking poles
* Warm layers, insulated jacket, gloves, and hat
* Waterproof/windproof outer layer
* Headlamp
* Lunch, snacks, and 2–3 liters of water

This is a challenging, high-altitude hike, especially in November. Come prepared for snow, ice, cold temperatures, and changing mountain weather.

🚗 **CARPOOLING & PARKING**

It's approximately a 2-hour drive from Denver, so carpooling is encouraged! AWD/4WD also highly encouraged!

**Meet**: Wooly Mammoth Park-N-Ride,
18560 US-40, Golden, CO 80401, USA · Golden, CO
Green benches near Section DD at Wooly Mammoth Park & Ride

**Depart:** 7:00 AM sharp

**Driving separately?** Plan to meet us at Glacier Gorge Trailhead at 9 AM.

The Glacier Gorge parking lot is small and may fill early. Since park shuttles aren't operating in November, we'll try the nearby Bear Lake Trailhead if Glacier Gorge is full. This adds roughly 0.5 miles each way to the hike.

**Passengers:** Please contribute toward gas and the park entrance fee.

🌨️ **WEATHER & SAFETY PLAN**

November weather in Rocky Mountain National Park is unpredictable, and snow or ice is likely at higher elevations.

**Snow or ice?** Bring microspikes and appropriate winter gear. Deep snow may require snowshoes.

**Timberline Falls unsafe?** We'll turn around rather than attempt an icy scramble.

**Severe weather, avalanche danger, or unsafe roads?** We'll choose a safer alternative or cancel.

**Final decision:** Friday, November 13, based on the latest weather forecast, trail conditions, and avalanche risk.

Looking forward to a great hike and meeting some new people!

SUMMARY: 🏓 Pickleball Social – All Levels Welcome! Make New Friends with Zhen !
DESCRIPTION:
Denver Fun Young Adults 20s to 40s
Ready to swap the couch for the court and make some awesome new friends?
Whether you’re a total beginner who just bought a paddle, an intermediate looking for a regular crew, or a seasoned expert ready to show off your spin, **this is your spot.**

we’re gathering for casual, social, and fun pickleball. No pressure, no judgment—just good vibes and great games.

\#\#\# 📍 Where to Find Us

* **Location:** Southpark Pickleball Complex
* we usually meet on courts 18 and 19
* **Address:** 400 W County Line Road, Highlands Ranch, CO 80129 *(Easy to find on GPS)*
* **Exact Spot:** Look for Zhen and a group of friendly people holding paddles near the courts or under the shade structures! Read comments to see what courts we are on.
* Text Zhen @ +19706319482 if you have any questions

\#\#\# 🕒 When

* Come when you can, leave when you must.

\#\#\# 👟 What to Expect

* **19 Outdoor Courts:** Plenty of space to play. Courts 18 & 19 are drop-in play, stack paddle play
* **All Skill Levels Welcome:** We love mixing beginners and intermediates to keep it social, but we can also set up competitive games for the experts.
* **Open Rotation:** We’ll rotate players after games so everyone gets a chance to play and meet new people.
* **First-Come, First-Served:** The courts are public and unreserved, so flexibility is the name of the game!

\#\#\# 🎒 What to Bring

* [ ] **Your Paddle** (If you don't have one, message us—someone might have a spare! I usually have a spare)
* [ ] **Water / Hydration**
* [ ] **Sunscreen & Hat** (Safety first!)
* [ ] **A Good Attitude**
* [ ] **Snacks to Share with Friends and Socialize**

SUMMARY: Running Group - Belleview Elementary School and Cherry Creek State Park
DESCRIPTION:
Denver Fun Young Adults 20s to 40s
**When and where**
We **leave** the Belleview Elementary School parking lot at **5:45 PM**, so please try to arrive a few minutes before then. If you are running late or can't find us, leave a comment or send a DM!

**Pace and distance**
Our typical run is around 4.5 miles at a steady 9-11:00 minute/mile pace. However, this varies depending on who shows up!

**Group size**
We usually have around 5-10 people attend, depending on the weather and season. Many of us have been coming for years; some people come every week, while others come less frequently.

**About us**
This is a small, dedicated running group that's been meeting consistently for several years (formerly under Colorado Runs). We're a friendly, tight-knit group that welcomes new members who are looking to make friends, train for races, or find consistent running partners.

Come join us if this sounds like a good fit for your running goals! We look forward to meeting you!
